feeds.title: MARTIN DUWELL Australian Poetry Review
feeds.description: The Australian Poetry Review is a blog dedicated to the review and discussion of Australian poetry. It features essays and reviews on a wide range of poems and poets, providing in-depth analysis and critique.

feeds.title: Australian Women Writers Blog » Poetry
feeds.description: There are a ton of poetry on the site written by different female poets. The website for Australian Women Writers launched in 2012. Its aim is to encourage reviews of novels written by Australian women. It aids in highlighting several writers from the past and present, such as numerous Indigenous authors, writers with disabilities, and Lesbian and Queer women writers. It focuses on authors from the 19th and the early to mid-20th centuries, including those who might not have attained fame during their lifetimes or whose writings have been lost or ignored due to historical gender prejudice.

feeds.title: Australian Poetry Hall Of Fame Blog
feeds.description: The Australian Poetry Hall of Fame preserves and celebrates Australian Languages, song-lines, poetry and prose in an archive accessible by all Australians. It nurtures and supports emerging and existing poets of Australia with opportunities to perform, competitions, publishing and education. It provides a regional arts and entertainment hub. Wade through the blog to become an international audience by providing opportunities to develop their art.

feeds.title: Australian Children's Poetry Blog
feeds.description: The blog is dedicated to showcasing contemporary Australian children's poets and their work. It features interviews with the poets, articles, and books. The blog contains poems based on nature, mysteries, different animals, and different seasons that are loved by the children. They are happy to accept information about children's poetry activities and events in Australia and overseas, poetry links, competitions, interviews with poets or publishers, and relevant articles.

feeds.title: PS Cottier
feeds.description: P.S. Cottier is a poet who occasionally writes prose. She have worked as a lawyer, a university tutor, a union organizer and a tea lady. She wrote on animals in the works of Charles Dickens, at the Australian National University, and also have a law degree from The University of Melbourne. She have judged poetry competitions, too, which probably puts her on a particularly interesting level of Dante's Inferno. She currently edit poetry for The Canberra Times, a newspaper. She shares her writings and experiences through her blog.

feeds.title: Australian Poetry
feeds.description: Australian Poetry was founded in 2011. It exists as a national poetry body to interconnect and support a flourishing community of Australian poets, to enhance and promote their poetry, here and internationally, and to reach and engage directly with readers, lovers and potential admirers of Australian poetry, and promoters of it. It acknowledges the critical funding support, organizationally, which it receives from the Australia Council for the Arts and Creative Victoria. Different poets turn to the blog to share their creations.

feeds.title: Kathryn Apel Blog
feeds.description: Kathryn Apel is a children's author and part-time literacy coordinator. She is the author of Fencing with Fear and she has had poetry and short stories published in children's magazines in Australia, New Zealand, and Canada. Kathryn specializes in poetry workshops for kids and adults - and staff professional development sessions across grades and curriculum area. She shares her poetry on her blog.

feeds.title: Meanjin » Poetry
feeds.description: Wade through the blog to encapasulate enticing poems. Meanjin was founded in 1940. It is where Australia's literary culture sets out its fiercest ambitions. It has fostered a rich and rigorous national conversation by remaining true to its founding principles: to talk poetry, to work for a healthy climate of opinion and literary activity, and to make clear the connection between art and politics. Each year it publishes new work by hundreds of Australian writers in all genres and forms.
